# Spreadsheets and tables

A sheet is a grid of cells for the calculations a design runs on (a load table, a clearance budget, a cut list, a building's areas) with intermediate rows that are not parameters of anything. It drives the model only through links you choose: any parameter can follow a cell.

- `sheet.create { name, description?, cells: { "A1": "Span", "B1": "2.4 m", "B2": "=B1 / 3", "B3": "=sum(B1:B2)" }, aliases?: { "B2": "rib_pitch" }, units?: { "B1": "m" } }`; `sheet.set { target, cells?, aliases?, units?, name?, clear? }` ("" or null empties a cell, removes an alias or unit). Both return the cells that show an error and why. Units: mm, cm, m, in, ft, deg, % (a bare 40 is 0.4) or number (a plain number). A formula in a cell with no unit takes one from what it does with what it reads: a length plus a length, or times or over a number, is a length; a length over a length is a plain ratio; what comes out of sin, cos, sqrt, ^ is a plain number; asin/acos/atan give angles.
- Cells hold what is typed: a number with an optional unit (`200`, `200 mm`, `1.2m`, `2in`, `45°`, `50%`; lengths are worked in mm, angles in degrees, and a cell shows its value in the unit it was written in or the cell's `unit`, which is also what a bare number typed there means), text (`'200` keeps a number as text), or a formula starting with `=`. Formulas are the parameter grammar (+ − × ÷ ^, min max abs round floor ceil sqrt sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sum average count mod pow hypot exp ln log pi, any case) plus cell references (`B2`, `$B$2`), ranges inside functions (`sum(B2:B9)`; empty and text cells skipped), aliases, and any parameter in the project (`=Desk.width / 2`, `=Other sheet.total`). Formulas work in mm; write units in them (`=B2 + 5mm`). A formula's result shows in the unit of the first length or angle it reads.
- Link a parameter to a sheet with `shape.link_param { target, key, expr: "=Sizes.rib_pitch" }` or `"=Sizes.B2"` (alias or address); references are stored by id, so renaming the sheet keeps them. A loop (the sheet reading what reads it) is refused. Errors stay in their cell (`#ERROR`, with the reason in the sheet's values); a parameter following a cell in error fails with that reason.
- In: `sheet.import { name | target, format: "csv" | "xlsx", text | base64, sheet?, at?: "C3", replace? }`. CSV fields come in as typed; Excel workbooks bring values, formulas Iṣẹ́ Studio reads (arithmetic, SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, ROUND…, filled shared formulas) and the workbook's names for single cells as aliases; formulas it cannot read (IF, text functions, other sheets) come in as their last value and are listed in `notes`. `parameters.import { name | target, format, text | base64 }` fills a parameter set from a table (header row key/name, value, unit, min, max, step, formula, label — or plain key, value, unit rows; values may carry units). `shape.config.import { target: shape, format, text | base64, active? }` makes a configuration table (first column the configuration names, then parameters by key or label, optional description, suppress, parts_off lists separated by `;`).
- Out: GET `/table/<id>.csv` or `.xlsx` for a sheet (CSV as each cell shows; the workbook keeps formulas that only read the sheet, aliases as defined names, numbers in mm and degrees), a parameter set, or a shape's configuration table. `./ise export Sizes sizes.xlsx` does it for you.
- The person has all of this in Data (T): sheets with a formula bar, aliases and units, import/export, parameter sets and configuration tables in and out.
